name: Do I need to seal the grout after installing kitchen tile?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to seal the grout after installing kitchen tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should seal your kitchen grout, especially in food preparation and high-traffic areas. Standard cementitious grout is naturally porous and absorbs cooking oil, sauce splatters, coffee, and water, which leads to staining and mildew buildup over time. Applying a penetrating grout sealer creates a protective barrier that keeps liquids on the surface for easy wiping. Natural stone tiles like marble also require sealing prior to and after grouting to prevent grout pigment from absorbing into the stone pores.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Cement-based grout is porous and absorbs cooking grease, food spills, and water. Sealer shields the grout lines from permanent staining and moisture.
